questions.question: Name the four rings of a flower from the outside inwards and state the function of each.
questions.expected_answer: Sepals: protect the flower when it is a bud. Petals: attract pollinators with colour, scent and nectar guides. Stamens: the male parts, which produce pollen containing male gametes. Carpels (pistil): the female parts, which receive pollen and contain ovules with female gametes.

questions.question: Name the parts of a stamen and of a carpel and give the function of each.
questions.expected_answer: Stamen: filament holds the anther in position; anther produces and releases pollen. Carpel: stigma receives and holds pollen (sticky, hairy or feathery); style holds the stigma up and connects it to the ovary; ovary contains the ovules, each with an egg cell.

questions.question: What do the ovules and ovary become after fertilisation? Explain why a mealie plant is said to have separate male and female flowers.
questions.expected_answer: Each ovule becomes a seed, and the ovary becomes the fruit. A mealie plant has male flowers in the tassel at the top, which produce pollen, and female flowers on the cob lower down; each silk is a style and stigma leading to one ovule, which becomes a grain.
